excluded.reason: the published source carries no room inventory, so the column is None on every offline row; excluded from the model matrix rather than fabricated or imputed

generation.note: Wall-clock and toolchain metadata only, outside the content checksum: re-running the pipeline must not look like a different result.

definitions.denominator: the number of observations for which a forecast was produced
definitions.mae: mean(|actual - forecast|) over evaluated observations; unit: room nights
definitions.rmse: sqrt(mean((actual - forecast)^2)) over evaluated observations; unit: room nights
definitions.skipped: observations for which the method could not produce a forecast; excluded from every metric above and reported separately, never counted as zero error
definitions.smape: 100 * mean(2 * |actual - forecast| / (|actual| + |forecast|)); a term whose denominator is zero (actual and forecast both zero, i.e. an exact match) contributes 0.0; range 0..200

model.baseline_definition: seasonal naive at a 7-day period: the forecast for (hotel, date) is the realised room nights for that hotel 7 days earlier, read from the dataset's own demand_lag_7 column -- the same weekday, the fewest whole weeks back the horizon allows. Where that observation does not exist the baseline produces no forecast; the day is counted as skipped and excluded from every metric.
model.name: demand_horizon

protocol.origin_rule: first origin = the date with minimum_train_days distinct dates at or before it; subsequent origins advance by step_days until the last dataset date; evaluation window = (origin, origin + horizon_days]
